passages.text: About that time there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
passages.sermon:
The people in Jerusalem cried out loudly.
Their wives also cried out.
They cried out against their fellow Jews.
This happened at that time.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֨י צַעֲקַ֥ת הָעָ֛ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם גְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶל־ אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: Some were saying, “We and our sons and daughters are numerous. We must get grain in order to eat and stay alive.”
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke.
They said, “We have many sons and daughters.
We are a large family.
We need to get grain.
We must eat.
We must live.”
passages.original: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים בָּנֵ֥ינוּ וּבְנֹתֵ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן וְנֹאכְלָ֥ה וְנִחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Others were saying, “We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our homes to get grain during the famine.”
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke.
They said, “We are mortgaging our fields.
We are mortgaging our vineyards.
We are mortgaging our homes.
We do this to get grain.
We need grain because there is a famine.”
passages.original: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים שְׂדֹתֵ֛ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֥ינוּ וּבָתֵּ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹרְבִ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן בָּרָעָֽב׃

passages.text: Still others were saying, “We have borrowed money to pay the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards.
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke.
They said, “We have borrowed money.
We needed this money to pay the king’s tax.
We used our fields and vineyards for this tax.”
passages.original: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים לָוִ֥ינוּ כֶ֖סֶף לְמִדַּ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׂדֹתֵ֖ינוּ וּכְרָמֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: We and our children are just like our countrymen and their children, yet we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved, but we are powerless to redeem them because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”
passages.sermon:
We are Israelites.
Our children are Israelites.
We are just like our fellow countrymen.
Our children are just like their children.
But we are making our sons slaves.
We are making our daughters slaves.
Some of our daughters are already slaves.
We cannot save them.
We have no power to help them.
Other people own our fields.
Other people own our vineyards.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּבְשַׂ֤ר אַחֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּשָׂרֵ֔נוּ כִּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם בָּנֵ֑ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֣ה אֲנַ֣חְנוּ כֹ֠בְשִׁים אֶת־ בָּנֵ֨ינוּ וְאֶת־ בְּנֹתֵ֜ינוּ לַעֲבָדִ֗ים וְיֵ֨שׁ מִבְּנֹתֵ֤ינוּ נִכְבָּשׁוֹת֙ וְאֵ֣ין לְאֵ֣ל יָדֵ֔נוּ וּשְׂדֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ לַאֲחֵרִֽים׃

passages.text: When I heard their outcry and these complaints, I became extremely angry, and after serious thought I rebuked the nobles and officials, saying, “You are exacting usury from your own brothers!” So I called a large assembly against them and said, “We have done our best to buy back our Jewish brothers who were sold to foreigners, but now you are selling your own brothers, that they may be sold back to us!” But they remained silent, for they could find nothing to say.
passages.sermon:
I am Nehemiah, the governor of the people.
I heard the outcry of the people.
I heard their complaints.
I became very angry.
I thought deeply about the situation.
I rebuked the nobles and the officials.
I said to them, “You are charging interest to your own brothers.”
I called a large assembly against them.
I said to them, “We have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to foreigners.”
“You are now selling your own brothers.”
“They must be sold back to us.”
The nobles and officials remained silent.
They could not find anything to say.
passages.original: וַיִּ֥חַר לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־ זַֽעֲקָתָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ וַיִּמָּלֵ֨ךְ לִבִּ֜י עָלַ֗י וָאָרִ֙יבָה֙ אֶת־ הַחֹרִ֣ים וְאֶת־ הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם מַשָּׁ֥א אִישׁ־ בְּאָחִ֖יו אַתֶּ֣ם נֹשִׁ֑אים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְהִלָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם אֲנַ֣חְנוּ קָ֠נִינוּ אֶת־ אַחֵ֨ינוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַנִּמְכָּרִ֤ים לַגּוֹיִם֙ כְּדֵ֣י בָ֔נוּ וְגַם־ אַתֶּ֛ם תִּמְכְּר֥וּ אֶת־ אֲחֵיכֶ֖ם וְנִמְכְּרוּ־ לָ֑נוּ וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹ֥א מָצְא֖וּ דָּבָֽר׃ס

passages.text: So I continued, “What you are doing is not right. Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God to avoid the reproach of our foreign enemies?
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader of the Jewish people.
He saw that some Jews were oppressing their own brothers and sisters.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, “What you are doing is not right.”
He told them to stop their wrong actions.
He asked, “Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God?”
He reminded them to respect and honor God.
He warned them to avoid bringing shame from foreign enemies.
He wanted them to act righteously before God and others.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא־ ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־ אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲל֞וֹא בְּיִרְאַ֤ת אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ תֵּלֵ֔כוּ מֵחֶרְפַּ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: I, as well as my brothers and my servants, have been lending the people money and grain. Please, let us stop this usury.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah is speaking to the people.
Nehemiah is a leader of the Jews.
Nehemiah says, “I have been lending money and grain to the people.
My brothers have also been lending money and grain.
My servants have done the same.
Let us stop charging interest.
Let us end this usury now.”
passages.original: וְגַם־ אֲנִי֙ אַחַ֣י וּנְעָרַ֔י נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶ֖ם כֶּ֣סֶף וְדָגָ֑ן נַֽעַזְבָה־ נָּ֖א אֶת־ הַמַּשָּׁ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Please restore to them immediately their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the percentage of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been assessing them.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Judah.
He spoke to the nobles and officials.
He said, "Return their property to the people today."
Give back their fields.
Give back their vineyards.
Give back their olive groves.
Give back their houses.
Return also the portion of money you charged them.
Return the grain you took from them.
Return the new wine you took from them.
Return the oil you took from them.
You demanded these things from your own people.
Now give everything back to them at once.
passages.original: הָשִׁיבוּ֩ נָ֨א לָהֶ֜ם כְּהַיּ֗וֹם שְׂדֹתֵיהֶ֛ם כַּרְמֵיהֶ֥ם זֵיתֵיהֶ֖ם וּבָתֵּיהֶ֑ם וּמְאַ֨ת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְהַדָּגָן֙ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: “We will restore it,” they replied, “and will require nothing more from them. We will do as you say.” So I summoned the priests and required of the nobles and officials an oath that they would do what they had promised.
passages.sermon:
The people replied to Nehemiah.
They said, “We will restore what we took.”
They said, “We will not demand anything more from the people.”
They said, “We will do as you say.”
Nehemiah called the priests.
Nehemiah made the nobles and officials take an oath.
He required them to do what they had promised.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ נָשִׁ֗יב וּמֵהֶם֙ לֹ֣א נְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כֵּ֣ן נַעֲשֶׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר וָאֶקְרָא֙ אֶת־ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וָֽאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, “May God likewise shake out of His house and possession every man who does not keep this promise. May such a man be shaken out and have nothing!” The whole assembly said, “Amen,” and they praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Judah.
He led the people during the time of King Artaxerxes.
Nehemiah made the nobles and officials promise to restore what they had taken from the poor.
I shook out the folds of my robe.
I said, “May God shake out every man who does not keep this promise.
May God remove him from his house and from what he has worked for.
May that man be left empty and with nothing.”
All the people in the assembly said, “Amen.”
They praised the LORD.
The people did what they had promised.
passages.original: גַּם־ חָצְנִ֣י נָעַ֗רְתִּי וָֽאֹמְרָ֡ה כָּ֣כָה יְנַעֵ֪ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֟ים אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ יָקִ֜ים אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּיתוֹ֙ וּמִ֣יגִיע֔וֹ וְכָ֛כָה יִהְיֶ֥ה נָע֖וּר וָרֵ֑ק וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ כָֽל־ הַקָּהָ֜ל אָמֵ֗ן וַֽיְהַלְלוּ֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָעָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Furthermore, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from his twentieth year until his thirty-second year (twelve years total), neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.
passages.sermon:
King Artaxerxes appointed me as governor in the land of Judah.
He did this in his twentieth year.
I served as governor until his thirty-second year.
This was a total of twelve years.
During these twelve years, I did not eat the food allotted to the governor.
My brothers also did not eat the food allotted to the governor.
passages.original: גַּ֞ם מִיּ֣וֹם׀ אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י לִהְי֣וֹת פֶּחָם֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָה֒ מִשְּׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֗ים וְ֠עַד שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֙יִם֙ לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֣סְתְּא הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁנִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה אֲנִ֣י וְאַחַ֔י לֶ֥חֶם הַפֶּ֖חָה לֹ֥א אָכַֽלְתִּי׃

passages.text: The governors before me had heavily burdened the people, taking from them bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people, but I did not do this because of my fear of God.
passages.sermon:
The governors before me ruled in Judah.
These governors placed heavy burdens on the people.
They took bread from the people.
They took wine from the people.
They also took forty shekels of silver from the people.
The servants of these governors also ruled harshly over the people.
I did not act like these former governors.
I did not burden the people.
I did not oppress the people.
I acted differently because I feared God.
passages.original: וְהַפַּחוֹת֩ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־ לְפָנַ֜י הִכְבִּ֣ידוּ עַל־ הָעָ֗ם וַיִּקְח֨וּ מֵהֶ֜ם בְּלֶ֤חֶם וָיַ֙יִן֙ אַחַר֙ כֶּֽסֶף־ שְׁקָלִ֣ים אַרְבָּעִ֔ים גַּ֥ם נַעֲרֵיהֶ֖ם שָׁלְט֣וּ עַל־ הָעָ֑ם וַאֲנִי֙ לֹא־ עָשִׂ֣יתִי כֵ֔ן מִפְּנֵ֖י יִרְאַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Instead, I devoted myself to the construction of the wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any land.
passages.sermon:
I am Nehemiah. 
I was the governor of Judah. 
I devoted myself to building the wall. 
All my servants worked with me on the wall. 
We did not buy any land.
passages.original: וְ֠גַם בִּמְלֶ֜אכֶת הַחוֹמָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ הֶחֱזַ֔קְתִּי וְשָׂדֶ֖ה לֹ֣א קָנִ֑ינוּ וְכָל־ נְעָרַ֔י קְבוּצִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם עַל־ הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃

passages.text: There were 150 Jews and officials at my table, besides the guests from the surrounding nations.
passages.sermon:
I am Nehemiah. I was the governor of Judah.
I invited people to my table.
There were 150 Jews and officials at my table.
There were also guests from the nations around us.
All these people ate at my table.
passages.original: וְהַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֜ים מֵאָ֧ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהַבָּאִ֥ים אֵלֵ֛ינוּ מִן־ הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ סְבִיבֹתֵ֖ינוּ עַל־ שֻׁלְחָנִֽי׃

passages.text: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and some fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. But I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on the people was so heavy.
passages.sermon:
I am Nehemiah. I was the governor of the people.
Each day, my servants prepared food for me.
They prepared one ox every day.
They prepared six choice sheep every day.
They also prepared some birds for me every day.
Every ten days, they brought me much wine of all kinds.
I did not ask for the food allowance given to governors.
The work was very hard for the people.
I did not want to add to their burden.
passages.original: וַאֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֗ד שׁ֣וֹר אֶחָ֞ד צֹ֠אן שֵׁשׁ־ בְּרֻר֤וֹת וְצִפֳּרִים֙ נַֽעֲשׂוּ־ לִ֔י וּבֵ֨ין עֲשֶׂ֧רֶת יָמִ֛ים בְּכָל־ יַ֖יִן לְהַרְבֵּ֑ה וְעִם־ זֶ֗ה לֶ֤חֶם הַפֶּחָה֙ לֹ֣א בִקַּ֔שְׁתִּי כִּֽי־ כָֽבְדָ֥ה הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה עַל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of the Jews in Jerusalem.
He led the people and cared for them.
He worked hard for their good.
He did not take the food or privileges of a governor.
He did this because the people already carried a heavy burden.
Nehemiah prayed to God.
He said, “My God, remember me for good.”
He asked God to remember all he had done for the people.
passages.original: זָכְרָה־ לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
